cards.summary: Qatar pursued talks in Tehran while another tanker attack was reported; Iran rejected Washington’s latest sanctions and the strait was not verified open.

cards.title: Ohio’s motor-voter injunction moves into appeal
cards.summary: The preliminary injunction remains the operative change at BMV offices while Secretary of State Frank LaRose pursues an immediate appeal.
detail: A federal judge’s Aug. 25 preliminary injunction blocks Ohio from relying on House Bill 54’s documentary-proof requirement before offering voter registration to eligible driver-license applicants at BMV offices. The order does not require an affirmative offer to applicants who identify as noncitizens or otherwise provide information showing they are not citizens.

Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose announced an immediate appeal, so the practical rule is now tied to litigation rather than a settled change in election administration. The court’s reasoning focused on the federal National Voter Registration Act and the added proof requirement.

The next uncertainty is whether the appeal changes the injunction before the Oct. 5 registration deadline. The state’s description of the case and the court’s order should remain separate: the injunction is verified, while the appeal’s outcome is not.
cards.why: The appeal is the material update to a ruling already affecting voter-registration practice.
verifiedFacts: A federal judge blocked enforcement of the BMV proof-of-citizenship requirement.
Ohio announced an immediate appeal.
attributedClaims: The Ohio Secretary of State said the order requires BMV registration materials to be offered even when citizenship cannot be verified.
analysis: The appeal keeps the registration process unsettled ahead of the midterms.
uncertainty: The appeal could alter the injunction before the registration deadline.

cards.title: Justice Department corrects scope of Chinese-hacking claims
cards.summary: The DOJ says QTFY targeted several U.S. agencies, then amended its release to distinguish targets from confirmed compromises.
detail: The Justice Department and FBI announced court-authorized seizures of the QScan and QTRouter domains on Aug. 26, describing a China-linked group called QTFY and a campaign targeting U.S. critical infrastructure. The department updated that release on Aug. 28 after correcting language that had described all named agencies as victims.

The distinction matters: the official record supports targeting across federal networks, but it does not establish that every agency listed was successfully hacked. Al Jazeera’s Reuters report likewise described the correction and said the Senate and Federal Reserve were targets rather than confirmed compromises.

The immediate action is technical disruption of the named platforms; the wider attribution and damage assessment remain claims grounded in an affidavit and agency statements. The next useful evidence is a fuller account of which systems were actually compromised and what indicators affected organizations should act on.

DOJ updated its release on Aug. 28 to distinguish targets from confirmed compromises.
attributedClaims: DOJ attributes QTFY to PRC-linked state-sponsored activity; the affidavit and agency statements support the targeting account.
Reuters reporting, republished by Al Jazeera, described the correction to the earlier release.
analysis: The correction lowers the certainty of a claim that every named agency was breached while leaving the targeting allegation in place.
uncertainty: The public materials do not provide a complete agency-by-agency compromise assessment.
